description: Normative statements no conformance vector can express, pinned by a named test in every runtime they apply to. Each runtime's test references the id verbatim; the SDK's consistency check asserts the reference exists. See the conformance suite spec, Harness.

statements.statement: Teardown observed while an action list is executing does not interrupt it: the list runs to completion, and only work arriving afterwards is refused.
On platforms with deterministic lifetimes, deallocation of the view counts as teardown: a completion arriving afterwards is dropped and reported.
The default node count (10,000) and document size (1 MiB) limits hold at their exact boundaries: at the limit builds, one over is LimitExceeded.
dispatchId is a string unique among every dispatch of every view in the process, whatever the views' labels; no two dispatches ever share one.
A state data provider failure during a replacement propagates to the caller unchanged, and the view is untouched: same document, same tree, same state, still serviceable.

Engine creation validates the vocabulary artifact and fails fast with InvalidVocabulary naming the rule the artifact violates, before any document is built. No vector can express it: a suite's engine is created from its vocabulary, so an invalid one has no vector to carry it.
A vocabulary artifact whose `milano` version the engine does not implement, by major or by minor, is rejected at creation as InvalidVocabulary with rule `milano-version`.
